learning_outcomes.text: The student must demonstrate the ability to classify and describe signals of interest for engineering, both in the time and frequency domains.
The student must demonstrate the ability to analyze simple signal processing schemes, particularly using linear systems.
The student must also demonstrate understanding of the random nature of many phenomena of interest for engineering and knowledge of the fundamental aspects of probability theory.
The student must demonstrate the ability to recognize problems that involve signal analysis and processing, choosing appropriate models for their description and solution.
The student must demonstrate the ability to design simple signal processing schemes, particularly using linear systems.
The student must also demonstrate the ability to model and solve simple random problems using the tools of probability theory.

syllabus_topics: Deterministic signals: continuous-time and discrete-time signals, energetic characterization of signals, Fourier series and transform, signal bandwidth.
Classification of systems: causality, stability, linearity, time-invariance.
Linear time-invariant systems: filtering in the time and frequency domains, system bandwidth, linear and non-linear distortion.
Random variables: complete and synthetic characterization of a variable, a pair of variables, a vector of random variables.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The written test includes numerical exercises.
